newsitem.title: UK: rugby union - Second Kiwi drafted into Welsh squad.
newsitem.headline: rugby union - Second Kiwi drafted into Welsh squad.

text.p: London, Dec 9 - New Zealand-born Dale McIntosh completed a convoluted path to international rugby when he was named today in the Wales team to play South Africa at Cardiff on Sunday.
The 27-year-old flanker was called into the Wales starting side today for the match against the world champions as a replacement for another New Zealand-born player, Cardiff's Hemi Taylor.

McIntosh, who like Taylor has Maori ancestry, is no stranger to British international rugby, having already turned out for Scotland A because of his Scottish heritage. Curiously, one of his appearances for Scotland A was against a Welsh under 21
selection, but he has now qualified for Wales after fulfilling the three-year qualification period with the Pontypridd club.
Hailing from the King Country, McIntosh makes his international debut on the blindside flank after impressing in that position for the Barbarians against Australia on Saturday.
He is one of four changes Wales coach Kevin Bowring has made from the side beaten by Australia a fortnight ago.

McIntosh and openside flanker Craig Charvis are new editions among the loose forwards, while veteran lock Mark Rowley has also been called up. And ace goalkicker Neil Jenkins is selected at fullback, enabling Jonathan Davies to keep the test No.10

Jenkins will assume the goalkicking duties, while there is still no room for Scott Quinnell, who is still in the middle of a pay dispute with the Welsh union. Quinnell's Richmond colleague Allan Bateman becomes the latest ex-rugby league player called up by Wales, earning a place on the replacements bench.
Bowring said the selection of Pontypridd pair McIntosh and Rowley is to give Wales much needed lineout presence, an area they were found wanting in against Australia.
At 1.82m and 16 stone, McIntosh adds bulk to the Welsh scrum as well.

"We needed players with an additional physical edge able to stamp their authority in the forward exchanges and on the game as a whole -- McIntosh, Charvis and Rowley fit into that category," Bowring said.
"Rowley has been a consistent performer during the past season and played very well against Olivier Roumat in the European Cup.
"In addition, his line-out partnership with McIntosh in the middle of the line could work to our advantage."
